title: T-107 Slice 0 — remove SequencerDirector P3-violating re-roll loop (single-draw anti-repeat)
description: First slice of the TASK-034 (GDD T-107) split (dev-t101 Phase A, orchestrator-ratified — needs no design ruling, so dispatched ahead of the human's mechanic rulings). Fixes the GDD Principle P3 violation confirmed in the TASK-035 review (rev-c035): SequencerDirector.cs:117-122 is a do-while that re-draws the microgame index until it gets a non-repeat — GDD §~506 P3 forbids nested randomness ('una decisión -> como máximo una tirada; prohibido objeto aleatorio que además falla aleatoriamente'). MINIMAL reading of TASK-034 comment-1 (rev-c035 scope addition): remove the re-roll loop only, preserving the anti-repeat guarantee via a filter-then-single-draw (build the candidate list excluding the last index, draw ONCE from it — the pattern MicrogameSelector V2 already uses), exactly one RNG draw per decision. Do NOT attempt the full Framework-wide v1->V2-selector swap here (SessionController/MicrogameLoopController/HudController/PlayerCornerHud reference v1 today; Sequencer.V2 has zero Framework consumers; the full swap is a TASK-055-scale wiring project) — file that as a separate follow-up ticket at hand-off. NOTE: draw-count/stream change may shift seed-pinned SequencerDirector tests — retune expectations with the single-draw rationale, do not just rebless.
acceptance_criteria: SequencerDirector's do-while re-roll loop (currently :117-122) is replaced by a filter-then-single-draw: the repeat-excluded candidate set is built first, then exactly ONE RNG draw selects from it — no decision takes more than one draw (GDD P3).
The anti-repeat guarantee is preserved (consecutive identical indices still cannot occur when >1 candidate exists) and pinned by a test; the degenerate single-candidate case is defined and tested.

Any seed-pinned SequencerDirector tests whose expectations shift due to the changed draw count are retuned with a documented single-draw rationale (not blind reblessing); tests-first for the new rule; red captured.
Fast suite green, no regression; a follow-up ticket is filed for the full Framework v1-SequencerDirector -> V2-MicrogameSelector production swap (out of scope here).

comments.author: dev-t101
comments.body:
Hand-off. Two commits, strict tdd order: 922e436 test(core) RED -> 46aff35 feat(core). Baseline 559 -> 561/561 (2 new tests).

SEED-STREAM BLAST RADIUS (the specific ask): SequencerDirector owns a FULLY DEDICATED RNG — verified by grep in both construction sites (MicrogameLoopController.BuildDirector() does `new SeededRandom(actualSeed)` solely for the director; SequencerTests.MakeDirector same). Nothing else reads or shares this instance, so changing PickNext's draw count has ZERO ripple into any other consumer's stream — unlike the TASK-044 PCG32 migration (which changed the algorithm under every shared/derived stream). Self-contained.

RED EVIDENCE (empirically measured): added a CountingRandom spy counting NextInt calls — against the unmodified do-while, 100 PickNext decisions on a 2-item pool consumed 190 draws (not 100), concretely confirming the P3 violation. Degenerate single-item pool already consumed 0 draws pre-ticket (existing special-case correct); added an explicit test locking that as intentional.

IMPL (AC1): replaced the do-while with the standard 'exclude one index from a uniform range' mapping — draw from [0, Count-1) (full range when _lastPickedIndex is -1), shift draws at-or-past the excluded index forward by one. Excluded index never produced, all others equally likely, exactly one RNG call per decision, no new allocation (pure-math, no candidate array). AC2 degenerate: Count==1 returns the only entry without touching RNG, [ASSUMED]-tagged (GDD §9.2 silent on a 1-pool), citing MicrogameSelector's own liveness-over-constraints precedent.

RETUNED TEST (AC3): PickNext_FixedSeed_ProducesExactDeterministicSequence (seed 42, 3-item pool) shifted from round 2 — expected (a 3+-item pool's old re-roll draw count was variable per round, so RNG trajectory diverges). NOT blind-reblessed: captured the actual new sequence (A,C,A,C,B,A,C,B,A,B) via a temp diagnostic, independently checked it has no consecutive repeat, wrote it in with an explanatory comment (mirroring the existing 'Recalibrated for TASK-044' comment in that test). Every OTHER test needed zero changes — verified, not assumed (2-item alternation is pigeonhole-forced; long-run + cross-instance tests assert algorithm-invariant structural properties). Mutation check: dropped the exclusion shift (idx=draw), 4 tests genuinely red incl. a caught anti-repeat violation ('Anti-repeat violated at round 7: C repeated after C'), proving the anti-repeat tests still do real work. Reverted before commit.

FOLLOW-UP DRAFTED (AC4, for orchestrator to file): full Framework v1-SequencerDirector -> V2-MicrogameSelector production swap — MicrogameSelector V2 has zero Framework consumers; SessionController/MicrogameLoopController/HudController/PlayerCornerHud all reference v1 today; a swap also means wiring the SessionStateMachine-based scoring into Framework production (not wired anywhere yet), likely bundled with TASK-055's fixed-60Hz Framework host. TASK-057's re-roll removal already satisfies comment-1's 'at minimum' on its own. Surface: SequencerDirector.cs + its tests only.
